# Workstation's palette bridge loses every token the theme declares

## Context

Reported by @tobiu 2026-08-31 against `dev@fa20136f29` (post `#17963`/PR `#17977`): *"looking into apps/workstation it looks exactly like 8h ago => no inline tab styling for the app."*

The report is correct, and the cause is not a missing stylesheet. Every sheet loads, every token the design pass shipped resolves, and the header actions project and gate exactly as designed. What fails is one layer lower: **Workstation's palette bridge is out-specified by the theme on the element the two share**, so the app renders the neo theme's neutral ramp instead of its own identity.

Measured live at `dev@fa20136f29` (dev server, `neo-theme-neo-dark`, 6 inline dock tab containers mounted). **21 of the bridge's 23 contested tokens lose. Zero win.**

## The Problem

`resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss:16` opens the bridge with `.workstation-viewport { … }` — 23 custom properties mapping generic `--grid-*` / `--tab-*` primitives onto the `--workstation-*` palette. Its own header states the intent: *"generic grid/tab primitives inherit its own palette in both skins instead of leaking their default blue/purple values."*

**The purple is leaking.** The rendered viewport element is:

```
div#neo-viewport-1.workstation-viewport.neo-viewport.neo-theme-neo-dark.neo-flex-container
```

It carries the app class **and** the theme class. So both of these match the *same element*:

| declaration | selector | specificity | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| bridge | `.workstation-viewport` | **(0,1,0)** | loses |
| theme | `:root .neo-theme-neo-dark` | **(0,2,0)** | **wins** |

Measured losses (bridge intent → what actually computes):

| token | bridge declares | computes to | theme source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--tab-indicator-background-color-active` | `--workstation-signal` `#5eead4` | `#FFFFFF` | `--cmp-tab-strip-selected` |
| `--tab-button-text-color` | `--workstation-ink-dim` `#8b97a8` | `#99A295` | `--sem-color-fg-neutral-subdued` |
| `--tab-button-glyph-color` | `--workstation-ink-dim` `#8b97a8` | `#99A295` | `--sem-color-fg-neutral-subdued` |
| `--tab-button-background-color-hover` | `color-mix(… signal 8% …)` | `rgba(255,255,255,.05)` | `--cmp-tab-unselected-bg-hover` |
| `--tab-button-background-color-active` | `color-mix(… signal 12% …)` | `rgba(255,255,255,.1)` | `--cmp-tab-unselected-bg-active` |
| `--grid-container-cell-background-color` | `--workstation-panel` `#141a23` | `#0E0F0D` | `--sem-color-surface-neutral-default` |
| `--grid-container-cell-background-color-even` | `--workstation-panel-2` `#1a212c` | `#11141C` | `--purple-950` |
| `--grid-container-border-color` | `--workstation-line` `#262f3d` | `#1D2E62` | `--purple-800` |
| `--grid-cell-background-color-hover` | `color-mix(… signal 10% …)` | `#182449` | `--purple-900` |
| `--grid-container-color` | `--workstation-ink-dim` `#8b97a8` | `#F0F2F0` | `--sem-color-text-neutral-default` |
| `--grid-header-button-justify-content` | `flex-end` | `start` | theme default |

…and 10 more, full list reproducible by the probe in the Evidence row below. **The active-tab indicator is white where the app's accent is mint, the grid renders on the theme's olive-black over purple borders where the app is blue-slate, and one loss is layout, not colour** (`justify-content`).

**A positive control proves the bridge is well-formed and only fails where contested.** The two tokens no theme declares — `--grid-cell-progress-active-color` and `--grid-cell-progress-track-color` — resolve to `#5eead4` and `#262f3d`, the workstation values, exactly as authored. The bridge is not broken; it is out-ranked.

**Two consequences are already compensated and are NOT part of this ticket's defect surface.** `Viewport.scss:172` re-declares the `--grid-header-button-*` family directly on `.neo-grid-header-button`, and that block wins — measured `#1a212c` / `#8b97a8` / `flex-end`, all correct. Those upstream declarations at line 27-36 are therefore dead, not wrong. The file already documents *why* that second block exists (`:168` — *"Theme classes live on the grid primitives themselves"*), which shows the collision was understood one element down and missed one element up.

### How it got here

`dda4aa04b4` (`#15923` / PR `#15928`, 2026-07-25) moved the bridge from `.workstation-workspace` to `.workstation-viewport` so the `?popout=` vessel — a viewport with no workspace — would reach it. That fix was correct for reachability and is not being reverted.

It also silently changed which side of the collision the bridge sits on, and nothing in the tree measured that:

- `.workstation-workspace` is **not** matched by `:root .neo-theme-neo-dark` (verified live: the workspace div carries `workstation-workspace neo-dock-workspace neo-flex-*` and no theme class). At that scope the bridge was the **only** matching declaration and won by default.
- `.workstation-viewport` **is** matched. At the new scope the bridge became the loser of a (0,1,0)-vs-(0,2,0) contest.

So the hoist traded a reachability defect for a specificity defect, and the app has been rendering theme paint ever since. `#17963`'s design pass did not cause this — it landed 8 new `--tab-header-*` tokens onto an app whose bridge was already inert, which is why the result reads as "nothing changed".

## The Architectural Reality

- **The bridge's mapping is skin-independent** (`--tab-button-glyph-color` → `--workstation-ink-dim`, whatever that resolves to per skin), so it correctly lives in the structural sheet `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss`, not duplicated per theme. Only its **selector** is wrong. The skin-dependent half — the `--workstation-*` values themselves — already lives correctly in `resources/scss/theme-neo-{dark,light}/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss`.
- **Moving the bridge into the theme layer is the wrong repair.** It would be emitted at `:root .neo-theme-neo-dark`, tying the theme's own (0,2,0) and resolving on load order. `#17241` names that exact hazard in this tree — *"Equal-specificity load-order ties are not a contract"* — and CSS is emitted per source file, so no readable source order decides it. A tie is not a fix.
- **The deterministic repair is a strictly-higher app selector that stays skin-agnostic.** `:root .workstation-viewport.neo-viewport` is (0,3,0): `:root` (0,1,0) + two classes. It beats the theme's (0,2,0) outright, names a real element (`neo-viewport` is the engine's viewport class, present in both boot modes), and needs no per-skin duplication.
- **Descendants that carry the theme class themselves are a separate case and are already handled.** A declaration matching an element directly beats any inherited value, so grid primitives — which do carry `neo-theme-*` — need the element-level block that `:172` already provides. The tab header toolbar and its buttons do **not** carry the theme class (nearest theme-classed ancestor is the viewport itself), so raising the viewport selector is sufficient for the whole tab surface.
- **The `--tab-header-*` family from `#17963` was never bridged at all** — it is 8 tokens newer than the bridge block and no one added rows for it. Even after the specificity repair those 8 stay theme-valued unless projections are authored.

## The Fix

`resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss` only. No engine change, no theme change, no JS.

1. **Raise the bridge selector** from `.workstation-viewport` to `:root .workstation-viewport.neo-viewport`, with an in-file comment recording the collision, the two specificities, and why the theme layer is not the home (the tie).
2. **Add the missing `--tab-header-*` projections** so `#17963`'s chrome speaks the instrument's language: glyph rest → `--workstation-ink-dim`, glyph hover/active → `--workstation-signal`, hover/active surfaces → the app's established `color-mix(… --workstation-signal …)` convention, and `--tab-header-inline-background-image` → a `--workstation-panel-2`-based band. The size and radius the theme ships are density decisions, not identity — leave them unless measurement says otherwise.
3. **Delete the now-dead `--grid-header-button-*` rows** at `:27-36` that `:172` already supersedes, or keep them and say in-file why both exist. One or the other — not silence.
4. **A computed-style spec** asserting the bridged tokens resolve to `--workstation-*` values, with a mutation control: removing the bridge block must red it. Grace's own sharpening on `#15923` applies directly — *"a class check would have passed throughout this entire bug"* — so the assertion reads computed values, never class presence.

No engine or theme surface changes. The engine's token names and the themes' values are consumed exactly as published.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029`. This is presentation-layer consumption inside one app; it neither challenges nor amends the docking design.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every token the bridge declares resolves to its `--workstation-*` intent on the live viewport element in **both** neo skins — asserted on computed values, not on class presence, and not on SCSS source.
- [ ] A mutation control: removing the raised bridge block makes the assertion red. Without it the spec observes the theme, not the promotion.
- [ ] The active-tab indicator renders `--workstation-signal`, and unselected tab label/glyph render `--workstation-ink-dim`, in both neo skins.
- [ ] The `--tab-header-*` family from `#17963` is projected onto the workstation palette; dock header action glyphs read the app's ink and signal, not `#99A295` / `#FFFFFF`.
- [ ] `--grid-header-button-*` computed values on `.neo-grid-header-button` are **unchanged** by this ticket — the element-level block at `:172` already wins, and the repair must not move it.
- [ ] The `?popout=` vessel keeps the reachability `#15923` bought: the bare-pane boot mode resolves the same bridged values as the workspace mode. This is the regression `#15928` was filed for and the raise must not undo it.
- [ ] No `!important` anywhere in the repair. If one seems required, the specificity cause is fixed instead (the discipline `#17241` recorded for the splitter promotion).
- [ ] The dense tour and the existing Workstation NL e2e battery still pass.

## Out of Scope

- **The general "should a theme out-specify its consumers" question.** That is the layering principle `#17241` owns; this ticket repairs one app deterministically and does not settle the engine-wide rule. If `#17241` later lands a general mechanism, this app's raise is the first thing it should delete.
- Any engine or theme SCSS change. The themes' values are correct for a theme; they are simply not this instrument's identity.
- The `--tab-header-action-{size,border-radius}` density values — theme-owned density, not app identity, unless a measurement in this lane says otherwise.
- Dock behaviour, action semantics, gating, ordering — all shipped and frozen by the `#13158` family leaves.
- `apps/agentos/fleet/FleetCockpit.scss`, whose own dock overrides belong to `#17241`.

## Avoided Traps

- **Reverting the `#15923` hoist.** It cured a real defect — the `?popout=` vessel rendering unskinned — and the workspace mode's regression is a *second* bug the hoist exposed, not a reason to restore the first. Both boot modes must resolve the bridge.
- **Moving the bridge into `theme-neo-*/apps/workstation/`.** It reads like the tidy home and it is a load-order coin flip against the theme's own (0,2,0). `#17241` already named this hazard in this tree.
- **Reaching for `!important`.** It would work, it would hide the specificity fact, and it would be copied by the next app. `#17241`'s splitter-promotion discipline is explicit that a needed `!important` is a specificity defect to fix, not a tool.
- **Asserting the fix with a class or selector check.** `#15923`'s post-mortem is the anchor: the theme class was never missing, so a class check passed for the entire lifetime of that bug. Only a computed-style assertion moves on the axis the defect moves.
- **Treating this as `#17963` shipping wrong.** `#17963`'s ACs were theme-layer and witness-layer, and PR `#17977` met them. The gap is one my own ticket did not name — it called Workstation a "living witness" and never asked whether the witness would speak the app's palette.
